thread.document:
What I did:

I ran an interactive, non-coding walkthrough of HW 3 using Gemini Pro. Full trace (screenshots + chat excerpts) is in my doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P6yTAFO4GR4W4a_l02kAFN2mYwKtmgsmPLecVg9gAGY/edit?tab=t.0

I used Gemini to sanity-check my derivations, clarify notation, and cross-validate with my own solutions

Workflow:

1) Try solo first (≤30 min). If blocked, paste the exact sub-question into Gemini.

2) Compare & probe. Check Gemini’s output against my derivation; ask for clarifications or for the missing step.

3) Tighten. Clarify equation statements, symbol mismatches, and ask for the key identity or rules explicitly.

Specific Example (Analogy + Clarification):

Topic: Interpreting pθ​:X→Δ(X) in Q4.

My Ask: “What does the arrow to Δ(X) mean in pθ​:X→Δ(X)?”

Gemini’s Analogy (helpful): Sound equalizer.

pθ​ = the equalizer; θ = slider positions;

X = the set of audible frequencies;

Δ(X) = all possible sound profiles (distributions over X).
 Changing θ selects a particular distribution in Δ(X).

My Follow-up (to make it precise): “Please restate without analogy: define X, Δ(X), and what an ‘element’ of Δ(X) is.”

Gemini (clarified): X is the sample space; Δ(X) is the set of all probability measures on X; for each θ, pθ​(⋅)∈Δ(X).

Pattern used: take the first pass (analogy/intuition), then demand the formal mapping with symbols.

Observations:

Uses analogies to simplify (e.g., equalizer for pθ​:X→Δ(X)). Helpful as a first pass.

Inconsistent symbols at times, likely from generic training patterns; needs nudging to match the homework question’s notation.

Positives (What Worked Well):

One-shot on standard rewrites: Correctly gave correct answers straight from around 30% of the questions

Right methodology even when imperfect: When wrong/incomplete, it still pointed in the correct direction

Negatives (Limitations and Effort Required):

Notation slippage: Misread or drifted symbols

Over/under-explanation: Wrapped easy steps in prose but skimmed tough steps unless I asked “elaborate on this step.”

Prompting Strategies That Helped:

“Derive further.” Ask for the exact algebraic substitution (e.g., show ∇p=p∇logp).

“Elaborate / Why this?” Request the chain-rule Jacobian or the gradient wrt input vs. parameters explicitly.

“Is my thought correct? If not, why?” Good for catching subtle mistakes and forcing a counterexample or fix.

“Show this equation more clearly” Keeps it concise and reduces misunderstanding

“Match the HW notation.” Prevents variable chaos.
